panels.title: Validation Send Rate [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often this node issues a ledger validation to the network. Each validation asserts the node fully validated one ledger.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of validation events sent, summed per node over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*A flat line at the network's ledger cadence is normal; higher is not better and lower means the node is validating less often.*

###### Healthy range:
*Roughly one validation per closed ledger (about 0.2-0.3/s on a healthy chain).*

###### Watch for:
*A drop to zero on a validator means it stopped validating; a value well below the close rate means validation is lagging.*

###### Keywords:
- **Ledger validation** *(network event)* — the second consensus stage where the node confirms a built ledger matches the trusted validator quorum and marks it final.
- **Ledger close interval** *(network-wide)* — the network's steady ledger rhythm — roughly one closed ledger every 3-5 seconds on Mainnet.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

###### Function:
`RCLConsensus::Adaptor::createValidationSpan`

###### References:
[Ledger validation](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/consensus-structure#validation) · [Ledger close interval](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/ledgers/ledger-close-times) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#ledger-validation)

panels.title: Consensus Mode Over Time
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Ledger-close activity split by the node's consensus mode (Proposing, Observing, Wrong Ledger, Switched Ledger).*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of ledger-close events grouped by consensus mode, per node, over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*One dominant band is normal; a validator should sit almost entirely in Proposing, a stock node in Observing.*

###### Healthy range:
*Nearly all activity in a single expected mode.*

###### Watch for:
*Sustained time in Wrong Ledger or Switched Ledger indicates the node is out of sync or flapping between chains.*

###### Keywords:
- **Ledger close** *(network event)* — the current open ledger is closed and a new closed ledger is built from the agreed transaction set.
- **Consensus mode** *(per node)* — the node's role/health in the current round: Proposing, Observing, Wrong Ledger, or Switched Ledger.
- **Consensus** *(network event)* — the protocol by which validators agree on the next ledger's transaction set and close time.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

###### Function:
`RCLConsensus::Adaptor::onClose`

###### References:
[Ledger close](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/ledgers/open-closed-validated-ledgers) · [Consensus mode](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/consensus-structure) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#ledger-close)

panels.title: Consensus Proposals Sent Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often this node proposes its candidate transaction set to peers during consensus.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of proposal-send events, summed per node over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*A steady line tracking the ledger cadence is healthy; only proposing (validator) nodes show activity.*

###### Healthy range:
*Steady output in step with the close rate for a proposing node; zero for a non-proposing node.*

###### Watch for:
*A proposing validator dropping to zero, or erratic spikes suggesting repeated re-proposals within rounds.*

###### Keywords:
- **Proposal** *(network event)* — a validator's advertised set of candidate transactions for the next ledger, revised each round.
- **Consensus** *(network event)* — the protocol by which validators agree on the next ledger's transaction set and close time.
- **Ledger close interval** *(network-wide)* — the network's steady ledger rhythm — roughly one closed ledger every 3-5 seconds on Mainnet.
- **Consensus mode** *(per node)* — the node's role/health in the current round: Proposing, Observing, Wrong Ledger, or Switched Ledger.
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

panels.title: Accept vs Close Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Two rates side by side: ledgers accepted after consensus versus ledger closes initiated.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of accept events and of close events, each summed per node over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*The two lines should overlap; read any gap between them as closes that did not finish accepting.*

###### Healthy range:
*Both lines equal and tracking the network close cadence.*

###### Watch for:
*A persistent gap where closes exceed accepts points to consensus rounds failing or timing out before acceptance.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus** *(network event)* — the protocol by which validators agree on the next ledger's transaction set and close time.
- **Ledger close** *(network event)* — the current open ledger is closed and a new closed ledger is built from the agreed transaction set.
- **Ledger close interval** *(network-wide)* — the network's steady ledger rhythm — roughly one closed ledger every 3-5 seconds on Mainnet.
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

###### Function:
`RCLConsensus::Adaptor::makeAcceptSpan / RCLConsensus::Adaptor::onClose`

panels.title: Validation vs Close Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Two rates side by side: validations sent versus ledger closes, so you can see whether every closed ledger gets validated.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of validation-send events and of close events, each summed per node over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*The lines should overlap; a validation line below the close line means validation is falling behind.*

###### Healthy range:
*Both lines equal at the network close cadence.*

###### Watch for:
*Validations persistently trailing closes, which means the node validates fewer ledgers than it closes.*

###### Keywords:
- **Validations checked vs sent** *(per node)* — validations this node received from peers and checked, versus validations it issued itself.
- **Ledger close** *(network event)* — the current open ledger is closed and a new closed ledger is built from the agreed transaction set.
- **Ledger close interval** *(network-wide)* — the network's steady ledger rhythm — roughly one closed ledger every 3-5 seconds on Mainnet.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

###### Function:
`RCLConsensus::Adaptor::createValidationSpan / RCLConsensus::Adaptor::onClose`

panels.title: Time to Reach Consensus (p50/p95)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Wall-clock time for the network to agree a ledger, at the median and 95th percentile.*

###### How it's computed:
*The recorded per-round agreement time is aggregated to its 50th and 95th percentile over the window.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; the p95 line shows the worst typical rounds while p50 shows the common case.*

###### Healthy range:
*Roughly 2-4 seconds on mainnet; workload- and network-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*Rising percentiles, or a p95 that pulls far above p50, signal slow or contentious rounds under load or poor peer connectivity.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.
- **Convergence time** *(network event)* — the wall-clock time the network took to agree a ledger in a round.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as trace spans and stored in Tempo; the value is computed directly from those raw spans by the panel's TraceQL query (no Prometheus metric involved).*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

###### Function:
`RCLConsensus::Adaptor::makeAcceptSpan`

###### References:
[Consensus round](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/consensus-structure) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#consensus-round)

panels.title: Average Time to Reach Consensus
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Mean wall-clock time for the network to agree a ledger.*

###### How it's computed:
*The recorded per-round agreement time averaged over the window.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; watch the trend rather than any single point.*

###### Healthy range:
*Roughly 2-4 seconds on mainnet; workload-dependent.*

###### Watch for:
*A steady upward drift indicates the network is taking longer to converge, often from load or connectivity problems.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.
- **Convergence time** *(network event)* — the wall-clock time the network took to agree a ledger in a round.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as trace spans and stored in Tempo; the value is computed directly from those raw spans by the panel's TraceQL query (no Prometheus metric involved).*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

###### Function:
`RCLConsensus::Adaptor::makeAcceptSpan`

###### References:
[Consensus round](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/consensus-structure) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#consensus-round)

panels.title: Consensus Rounds per Ledger (Establish Count)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many establish-phase iterations each ledger needed before validators converged.*

###### How it's computed:
*Ledgers are counted over the window and grouped by their iteration count; each series is one count value.*

###### Reading it:
*Most weight on the '1' series is ideal; weight shifting to 2, 3 or more shows harder convergence.*

###### Healthy range:
*The large majority of ledgers converging in one iteration.*

###### Watch for:
*A growing share of ledgers needing several iterations, indicating disagreement or network stress.*

###### Keywords:
- **Establish phase** *(network event)* — the consensus phase where validators iterate proposals; the establish count is how many iterations a ledger needed.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as trace spans and stored in Tempo; the value is computed directly from those raw spans by the panel's TraceQL query (no Prometheus metric involved).*

###### Source:
[Consensus.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/consensus/Consensus.h)

###### Function:
`Consensus::startEstablishTracing`

###### References:
[Establish phase](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/consensus-structure) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#establish-phase)

panels.title: Previous Round Time per Ledger
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Duration of the immediately preceding consensus round, at the 95th percentile.*

###### How it's computed:
*The prior round's recorded duration is aggregated to its 95th percentile over the window.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; complements the time-to-consensus panels with the previous round's cost.*

###### Healthy range:
*Comparable to the current time-to-consensus, roughly a few seconds.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising p95 means recent rounds have been expensive, often preceding a slowdown in ledger cadence.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.
- **Convergence time** *(network event)* — the wall-clock time the network took to agree a ledger in a round.
- **Consensus** *(network event)* — the protocol by which validators agree on the next ledger's transaction set and close time.
- **Ledger close interval** *(network-wide)* — the network's steady ledger rhythm — roughly one closed ledger every 3-5 seconds on Mainnet.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as trace spans and stored in Tempo; the value is computed directly from those raw spans by the panel's TraceQL query (no Prometheus metric involved).*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

###### References:

panels.title: Close-Time Resolution Change (per Round) [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Whether the close-time rounding granularity moved Coarser, Finer, or stayed Steady versus the previous round.*

###### How it's computed:
*Rounds are counted over the window and grouped by direction of change.*

###### Reading it:
*Mostly Steady is healthy; Coarser means widening bins (more disagreement), Finer means tightening.*

###### Healthy range:
*Predominantly Steady.*

###### Watch for:
*Frequent Coarser shifts indicate the network is repeatedly failing to agree on close time.*

###### Keywords:
- **Close-time resolution** *(network event)* — the granularity (in seconds) that close times are rounded to; widens when validators disagree.
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.
- **Close time** *(network event)* — the timestamp validators agree to stamp on a ledger, rounded to a shared resolution.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as trace spans and stored in Tempo; the value is computed directly from those raw spans by the panel's TraceQL query (no Prometheus metric involved).*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

###### Function:
`RCLConsensus::Adaptor::doAccept`

###### References:
[Close-time resolution](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/ledgers/ledger-close-times) · [Consensus round](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/consensus-structure) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#close-time-resolution)

panels.title: Close-Time Proposal Spread (Distinct Positions per Round) [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How spread out validators' proposed close times were, as the number of distinct positions per round.*

###### How it's computed:
*Rounds are counted over the window and grouped by their distinct-position count; each bar is one count value.*

###### Reading it:
*Weight on '1 distinct position' means everyone agreed; weight on 2 or more means the proposals split.*

###### Healthy range:
*Most rounds at a single distinct position.*

###### Watch for:
*A shift toward two or more distinct positions signals growing clock drift or latency across validators.*

###### Keywords:
- **Distinct positions** *(network event)* — the number of different close-time values validators proposed in a round; one means full agreement.
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.
- **Proposal** *(network event)* — a validator's advertised set of candidate transactions for the next ledger, revised each round.
- **Clock drift** *(network event)* — differences between validators' clocks, which spread their proposed close times.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as trace spans and stored in Tempo; the value is computed directly from those raw spans by the panel's TraceQL query (no Prometheus metric involved).*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

###### Function:
`RCLConsensus::Adaptor::doAccept`

###### References:
[Distinct positions](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/ledgers/ledger-close-times) · [Consensus round](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/consensus-structure) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#distinct-positions)

panels.title: Position Update Duration
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Time this node spends each round tallying disputes and updating its consensus position, at the 95th percentile.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-round position-update durations are aggregated to their 95th percentile over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; short, flat durations are normal.*

###### Healthy range:
*A few milliseconds under normal load.*

###### Watch for:
*Sustained high durations point to heavy dispute resolution or slow convergence on close time.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.
- **Position update** *(per node)* — the per-round work of tallying disputes and revising the node's own consensus position.
- **Close time** *(network event)* — the timestamp validators agree to stamp on a ledger, rounded to a shared resolution.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[Consensus.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/consensus/Consensus.h)

###### Function:
`Consensus::updateOurPositions`

panels.title: Ledger Close Duration
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Full consensus round duration (open to accept) at the 95th percentile — the time a ledger takes to close.*

###### How it's computed:
*95th percentile of the consensus.round span duration per node over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*Tracks the network close interval (~3-5s on mainnet); lower and steadier is better.*

###### Healthy range:
*A few seconds, matching the close cadence; workload-dependent on test networks.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising p95 means rounds are taking longer to converge.*

###### Note:
*Uses consensus.round, not consensus.ledger_close: the latter span only wraps the sub-millisecond onClose() prologue and is not the ledger close time.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.
- **Consensus** *(network event)* — the protocol by which validators agree on the next ledger's transaction set and close time.
- **Ledger close interval** *(network-wide)* — the network's steady ledger rhythm — roughly one closed ledger every 3-5 seconds on Mainnet.
- **Convergence time** *(network event)* — the wall-clock time the network took to agree a ledger in a round.
- **Ledger close** *(network event)* — the current open ledger is closed and a new closed ledger is built from the agreed transaction set.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

`RCLConsensus::Adaptor::onClose (round span)`

panels.title: Ledger Apply Duration (doAccept)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Time spent applying the agreed transaction set to build the new ledger, at the 95th percentile.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-apply durations are aggregated to their 95th percentile per node over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; this is the cost of executing the ledger's transactions.*

###### Healthy range:
*A few to tens of milliseconds, scaling with the number of transactions in the ledger.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising p95 alongside high transaction counts signals apply-stage load, whether organic or from a flood of transactions.*

###### Keywords:
- **Transaction apply phase** *(per node)* — the step that executes the agreed transaction set into the new ledger during a close.

###### Computation boundary:

###### Keywords:

panels.title: Close-Time Agreement Rate (Agreed vs Disagreed)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often validators agreed on the ledger close time versus agreed to disagree.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of rounds split into Agreed and Disagreed, per node, over the rate interval.*

###### Reading it:
*Mostly Agreed is healthy; occasional Disagreed is normal when validator clocks differ slightly.*

###### Healthy range:
*Overwhelmingly Agreed.*

###### Watch for:
*A sustained rise in Disagreed points to clock drift or latency spread across the validator set.*

###### Keywords:
- **Ledger close** *(network event)* — the current open ledger is closed and a new closed ledger is built from the agreed transaction set.
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.
- **Clock drift** *(network event)* — differences between validators' clocks, which spread their proposed close times.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

###### Source:

panels.title: Close Time Vote Bins & Resolution
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Two related values: how many distinct close-time votes were seen, and the current close-time rounding granularity in ms.*

###### How it's computed:
*Both values are averaged over the window and plotted on dual axes.*

###### Reading it:
*Fewer vote bins and a fine resolution mean tight agreement; more bins and a coarse resolution mean disagreement.*

###### Healthy range:
*Few bins with a fine (about 10s) resolution.*

###### Watch for:
*Rising bins with the resolution widening (toward 120s) shows validators struggling to agree on close time.*

###### Keywords:
- **Distinct positions** *(network event)* — the number of different close-time values validators proposed in a round; one means full agreement.
- **Close-time resolution** *(network event)* — the granularity (in seconds) that close times are rounded to; widens when validators disagree.
- **Close time** *(network event)* — the timestamp validators agree to stamp on a ledger, rounded to a shared resolution.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as trace spans and stored in Tempo; the value is computed directly from those raw spans by the panel's TraceQL query (no Prometheus metric involved).*

###### Source:
[RCLConsensus.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/consensus/RCLConsensus.cpp)

###### Function:
`RCLConsensus::Adaptor::doAccept`

[Distinct positions](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/ledgers/ledger-close-times) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#distinct-positions)

panels.title: Consensus Outcome Distribution (per Round)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How consensus rounds concluded: Agreed, Moved On (partial), Expired (timeout), or No Consensus.*

###### How it's computed:
*Rounds over the window are counted and grouped by outcome, shown as shares of a pie.*

###### Reading it:
*An almost fully Agreed pie is healthy; other slices represent degraded outcomes.*

###### Healthy range:
*Nearly 100 percent Agreed.*

###### Watch for:
*A growing Moved On or Expired share signals network stress, disagreement, or connectivity loss.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus round** *(network event)* — one propose-and-revise iteration of consensus; several may run before validators converge on a ledger.
- **Consensus outcome** *(network event)* — how a round concluded: Agreed, Moved On (partial), Expired (timeout), or No Consensus.

*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in code as a trace span, turned into a metric by the collector (SpanMetrics connector), then aggregated by the Grafana query.*

panels.title: Consensus Failures Over Time

###### What this is:
*Rate of non-normal consensus outcomes (moved-on plus expired) over time.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of the moved-on and expired outcomes, summed per node over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*Flat at zero is healthy; any sustained line is a concern.*

*Zero under normal operation.*

###### Watch for:
*Spikes or a persistent nonzero rate indicate consensus instability that can precede ledger stalls or forks.*

panels.title: Consensus Stall Rate

###### What this is:
*Rate at which consensus health checks report a stalled condition versus not stalled.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of consensus checks split by stalled flag, summed per node over a 5-minute window.*

*The Not Stalled line should carry all the weight; any Stalled line is an early warning.*

*Stalled at zero.*

###### Keywords:

panels.title: Consensus Mode-Change Rate by Target Mode
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often the node switches consensus mode, broken down by the mode it switched into.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second rate of mode-change events grouped by target mode, per node, over a 5-minute window.*

###### Reading it:
*Near-zero is healthy; a stable node rarely changes mode.*

###### Healthy range:
*Essentially zero mode changes in steady state.*

###### Watch for:
*Frequent switches into Wrong Ledger or Switched Ledger mark an unstable node at risk of forking.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus mode** *(per node)* — the node's role/health in the current round: Proposing, Observing, Wrong Ledger, or Switched Ledger.
- **Fork** *(network-wide)* — when nodes validate divergent ledger chains instead of a single agreed history.

panels.title: Ledger History Mismatch Rate by Reason

###### What this is:
*Rate of built-versus-validated ledger mismatches, broken down by why they diverged.*

###### How it's computed:

*Flat at zero is healthy; the reason label tells you the nature of any divergence.*

*Any sustained rate marks a fork; the reason distinguishes close-time disagreement, sync drift, and transaction-processing differences.*

- **Close time** *(network event)* — the timestamp validators agree to stamp on a ledger, rounded to a shared resolution.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (MetricsRegistry, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

description: What this shows: Consensus health for XRPL nodes: how reliably and quickly the network agrees each ledger, and where agreement breaks down.  —  Use it to: Spot stalled or slow consensus rounds and pinpoint the phase where agreement is failing.
